Hi Alex / Priya (copying Rishi + Vivek for technical follow-up),

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about FinTechCo's ingestion pipeline and the security requirements you need for production inference. Recap of the key asks we captured: 

- Logging retention: request/response logs and metadata retained for 90 days by default; FinTechCo prefers 180 days for audit.
- Sensitive data: redaction/masking required for PII (emails, SSNs), payment details (PAN), auth headers, and internal trace IDs when logs leave the secure environment.
- Headers & trace IDs: you want assurance that Authorization/Set-Cookie headers are not persisted and trace IDs can be scrubbed or tokenized.
- Data residency: logs must be stored in US-only regions for this initial rollout.

Next steps we propose: 
1) I’ll attach our SOC2 overview + a short logging/redaction patterns doc for your security team to review (attached).
2) Please share 2–3 sanitized example payloads (we only need samples of request/response shapes) so Rishi can validate redaction rules against your schema.
3) Schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive with your security/infra and our infra team (Rishi/Vivek) next week to confirm where redaction happens (ingest vs. storage) and validate retention windows.

Technical clarifications up-front: our hosted API does capture request/response metadata for observability. We support configurable redaction rules (regex + field-level mapping) that are applied pre-storage. For customers who require stronger guarantees, Dedicated and Private deployments give you options to disable persistence of response bodies entirely and to host logs in a customer-controlled region.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_overview.pdf, logging-redaction-patterns.docx

Proposed meeting times: Mon 11/23 10:00–10:30 PT or Tue 11/24 14:00–14:30 PT. Tell me what works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few clarifying Qs before we share payloads: 

1) Trace IDs: are those ever written to long-term logs by default (i.e., do you persist X-Trace-ID or equivalents in request/response logs)? We need to ensure traceability without exposing internal correlation IDs externally.
2) Headers: do you strip Authorization/Set-Cookie by default or is that left to customer-configured redaction rules?
3) Masking: do you support both deterministic hashing and full redaction? For payment PANs we need one-way tokenization (non-reversible) for downstream troubleshooting.
4) Where does redaction run — at the API gateway (ingest) or at the storage layer?

Also, can you confirm whether your hosted logs are stored in an encrypted S3-like object store and whether KMS keys are customer-managed in the Private option?

If you can answer these quickly we’ll prep sanitized sample payloads and propose a time for the deep dive.

Hi Alex — thanks for the questions, answered inline below. I’ve also looped in Rishi (infra) and Neha (product) to help with any follow-ups.

1) Trace IDs: by default we capture trace IDs in request metadata to support tracing and debugging, but they are not tied to customer-identifying data. We can provide a configuration to scrub or replace trace IDs with hashed tokens before they're written to persistent logs. For Private deployments you get full control to never persist trace IDs.

2) Headers: Authorization, Cookie, and other sensitive headers are covered by our default redaction rules but customers should still verify. We apply a default header blacklist that strips common auth headers; customers can add additional header patterns.

3) Masking/tokenization: we support multiple redaction actions — full redact (replace with [REDACTED]), deterministic SHA256 hashing, and one-way tokenization integrated with our token service (suitable for PCI-like requirements). The one-way tokenization option is available for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers can use deterministic hashing or full redact.

4) Redaction execution point: redaction runs at ingestion in the runtime pipeline (pre-storage) so sensitive fields never hit long-term storage if configured that way. We also support a storage-time policy for legacy datasets.

Encryption/KMS: hosted logs are encrypted at rest using Redwood-managed keys by default. For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and HSM integrations for enterprise plans.

Attached is a short doc (logging-redaction-patterns.docx) that details default rules and recommended regex patterns. Rishi — can you take a look at the sample payloads once Alex sends them and flag any edge cases? Vivek/Neha — happy to cover deployment options during the deep-dive.

Proposed: Mon 11/23 10:00 PT works for us — I’ll send an invite for a 30-min deep-dive.

Regards,
Marissa
